title: Maximizing the ROI of a Second Home: Why Location Matters

# Maximizing the ROI of a Second Home: Why Location Matters


Tri Pointe Homes


•


November 17, 2026


Share this article


A second home can be more than a weekend escape. With the right location and strategy, it can become a flexible asset that provides personal enjoyment, potential rental income and long-term value. The key is choosing a home in a location where people already have plenty of reasons to visit.


For those considering a second home in the Triangle, Chapel Hill offers a compelling combination of university life, year-round attractions, outdoor recreation, dining and easy access to surrounding communities. With its convenient location near the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill,[Summit at Homestead by Tri Pointe Homes](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/raleigh/summit-at-homestead) ® puts second-home owners close to many of the experiences that make the area a destination in its own right.


**Start With a Location That Has Built-In Demand**


One of the biggest factors to consider when purchasing a second home is location. A beautiful property may not deliver the same value if it is far from the places people want to visit. Instead, look for communities near universities, medical centers, entertainment, restaurants, outdoor recreation and other attractions that create consistent demand throughout the year.


Summit at Homestead is located in Chapel Hill, a town that checks many of those boxes. It is home to[UNC-Chapel Hill](https://www.unc.edu/) and[UNC Health,](https://www.unchealth.org/home) one of the nation’s[leading academic health care systems](https://www.northcarolina.edu/institution/unc-health-care-system/) . A[vibrant downtown](https://www.downtownchapelhill.com/) adds to the appeal with local restaurants, shops and entertainment. The surrounding area also puts residents within easy reach of Carrboro, Durham, Hillsborough and the greater Triangle.


That steady stream of visitors is reflected in the area’s tourism economy. In 2024, visitors spent more than[$280 million in Orange County, a 4.9% increase](http://visitchapelhill.org/articles/post/2024-visitors-spending-in-orange-county-nc-more-than-280-million/) from 2023. UNC athletics is another major draw, bringing visitors to the area throughout the year.


For a second-home owner, that means choosing a location where there are already plenty of reasons for people to come, and plenty of reasons for you to want to come back, too!


**Make the Most of Major Events and Game Days**


For a Carolina fan, owning a second home near campus can add another layer of value. Instead of planning a game-day trip around hotel availability, a second home can provide a familiar place to gather with alumni and friends throughout the athletic seasons.


But the appeal doesn’t have to end when the game is over. Graduation weekends, family visits, campus events and other university activities bring visitors to the area year-round. For owners who plan to rent their second home when they aren’t using it, these seasons and events may offer opportunities to offset some ownership costs.


**Look Beyond Rental Income**


While rental income can be one consideration when purchasing a second home, it shouldn’t be the only measure of its return.


A second home can provide a place for group gatherings, weekend getaways or extended stays. It could eventually become a retirement destination or a home base for spending more time in the Triangle. Some owners may even explore home-exchange opportunities that turn unused time in their property into travel value elsewhere.


The more ways a property can fit into your life, the more chances you have to get value from it! That’s especially true when the home is in a location you genuinely enjoy visiting.


**Look for Year-Round Value**


The strongest second-home opportunities aren’t dependent on one event or one season. Instead, they offer reasons to visit throughout the year.


In Chapel Hill, that could mean football in the fall, basketball in the winter, springtime visits to explore the area’s[parks](https://www.chapelhillnc.gov/Events-and-Activities/Find-a-Park-or-Greenway/Parks) and[trails](https://www.chapelhillnc.gov/Events-and-Activities/Find-a-Park-or-Greenway/Greenways) ,[activity-filled summer weekends,](https://www.visitchapelhill.org/blog/post/top-summer-festivals-and-events-in-chapel-hill-and-orange-county-nc/) celebrations or university events.


That year-round appeal can make a second home more versatile. When you’re not using it for a weekend getaway, it may have potential to serve another purpose, whether that’s hosting friends or colleagues, accommodating visitors or generating rental income.


**Make Second-Home Ownership Easier**


A low-maintenance townhome can be particularly appealing for those looking to simplify second-home ownership.[Summit at Homestead](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/raleigh/summit-at-homestead) offers thoughtfully designed three- and four-bedroom townhomes ranging from 1,767 to 2,146 square feet, with two to three bathrooms and attached garages. Community amenities, including gathering spaces and a dog park, give residents opportunities to enjoy the neighborhood close to home.


Whether you’re looking for a home base for Carolina game days, a place to gather, or a second property with potential for long-term value, Summit at Homestead offers a way to make your time in Chapel Hill count, both now and for years to come!
